E2
Bench test 1: power, no servos yet

☐1LIZVOR adapter, nothing connected, plain 5.5 × 2.1 mm tipDisplay + meter on the tip (centre = +)12.0 V, centre positive. Tape the knob
☐2Adapter → terminal-block tip → buck IN+ / IN−Buck display / meter on OUT+ / OUT−Turn the buck pot (many turns) to 5.8 V. Dot of nail polish on the pot
☐3Buck OUT → breadboard + / − rails. 1000 µF capacitor across the railsStripe on the capacitor = − railRail reads 5.8 V

☐5bUno GND → rail − (common ground: required)Meter between Uno GND and the buck OUT−0 Ω / beeps

Never connect the rail (5.8 V) to the Uno's 5V pin. The Uno gets its power only from the 9 V battery (jack or VIN); the 12 V adapter feeds only the buck. The 1000 µF capacitor is optional while testing: skip row 3 if you don't have one yet, and fit it before the final runs.

E3
Bench test 2: one servo at a time (firmware/bench_test)

Plug only the servo for the next test. Brown = GND (rail −), red = + (rail +), orange = signal (pin). The MG996R's + / − go to the buck OUT terminals (cut extension), its signal to D9.

TestServoPlug signal toPress START, expect
☐1SG90 gripperD5Goes to 20°, wiggles ±10°, back
☐2MG90S wristD60°, wiggle to 20°, then a full half-turn 0 → 180 → 0: mark the horn and check it really reaches 180°
☐3MG90S liftD1030°, wiggles ±10°
☐4MG996R turntableD9 (+/− on the buck)135°, wiggles ±10°
☐5All four plugged in—All at HOME for 5 s. Meter on the rail: stays above 5.5 V

Each test: smooth, no buzzing, the Uno doesn't reset (no 3× blink in the middle).

E3b
Laptop control panel (viewer/control_panel.html)

1. Upload firmware/concept_a/concept_a.ino with the Arduino IDE, then close the IDE's Serial Monitor (only one program can use the USB port). 2. Open viewer/control_panel.html in Chrome or Edge (or the project site link). Click Connect to Arduino and pick the Uno's port. The Uno restarts; after ~2 s the angles appear. 3. Each servo has a slider, ±5° buttons and its working angles (base START 135° / TARGET 45°, lift DOWN / UP, wrist UPRIGHT / FLIPPED, grip OPEN / RELEASE / CLOSED). Every move is smooth and stays inside safe limits. 4. HOME brings the robot home one servo at a time. START runs the whole sequence (same as the physical button, which keeps working). START only runs from HOME. STOP (or Esc) holds where it is.

CheckExpected
☐Each servo buttonOnly that servo moves, to that angle, smoothly
☐HOMELift up → wrist → base → grip → lift down
☐START at HOMEGRIP → LIFT → FLIP → TURN → LOWER → RELEASE, ends DONE
☐START again after DONE (can removed)Goes home
☐STOP during a moveHolds; HOME before the next START

Tested without hardware: the firmware's commands on a simulated Uno (backend/tools/firmware_test/run.sh, 15 checks) and the page driving the live firmware through a fake USB port (panel_test.js, 11 checks).

E4
If something is wrong
SymptomLikely causeFix
☐Uno resets (blinks 3×) when a servo moves9 V battery flat, or the servo supply wired to the Uno by mistakeBattery < 7.5 V: replace it. Check nothing from the rail goes to the Uno's 5V or VIN
☐Servos twitch or don't respond at allNo common groundUno GND ↔ rail − (row 5b)
☐Servo buzzes / jittersSignal without ground, loose jumperRe-seat; shorter jumpers; ground first
☐Servo doesn't move at allSignal on the wrong pin, dead servoSwap the plug to a known-good test; try the spare
☐Wrist stops short of 180°That MG90S's rangeservo_setup: try WRIST_MIN_US / WRIST_MAX_US 450 / 2550; else swap MG90S (buy a spare)
☐Rail below 5.5 V in test 5Weak adapter / long thin wires / no capacitorShorter rail wires; check the adapter is at 12.0 V under load; fit the 1000 µF
☐Buck gets hotPot set too high, shortUnplug, re-check OUT = 5.8 V with nothing connected
E5
Wiring dry run (decides what to return)

With the servos still loose, build the jumper chains (prototype v1 BOM): 2 jumpers per wire for the gripper, 1 for the wrist and lift, tape every joint. Re-run tests 1–5 through the chains.

• All pass, joints stay put when you tug and bend them → return the extension leads.
• A joint drops out or a servo resets → keep the extension leads.

Record the results (angles that looked right, rail voltage in test 5) in the build log: they go in the report's test section.

Then: PART M, the mechanics

Print plates 0–3 (cad/print/plates), then follow steps 1–23. Keep the bench-test wiring: it moves into the tray in step 21.
